nodes.name: Coat 01
nodes.speaker: Mk-II
nodes.dialogue: The community hall wall is dark blue, scuffed, and exactly the shade of an old regret.{pause}Mk-II arrives carrying three cans of white paint stacked higher than his helmet crest.{pause}He says he understands repainting better than anyone and refuses to explain the emphasis.{pause}GM has brought two brushes, one drop cloth, and the optimism of a volunteer coordinator.

nodes.name: Coat 02
nodes.speaker: GM
nodes.dialogue: The supply list requested two cans, but you brought a third marked EMOTIONAL RESERVE.{pause}Mk-II calls it contingency coverage and places it where nobody can accidentally open it.{pause}The lid immediately pops loose because the can was balanced on a folding chair.{pause}GM catches it with a roller tray and gains confidence for nearly four seconds.

nodes.name: Coat 03
nodes.speaker: SYSTEM
nodes.dialogue: Mission: turn one dark-blue wall into a calm white wall before movie night.{pause}Secondary mission: keep paint off the floor, chairs, curtains, snacks, and each other.{pause}Mk-II adds a third mission involving complete chromatic redemption and perfect edge lines.{pause}GM quietly circles the words keep paint off each other twice.

nodes.name: Coat 04
nodes.speaker: Mk-II
nodes.dialogue: Preparation begins with tape placed along the ceiling in a single unbroken line.{pause}Mk-II reaches easily, but his shoulder catches the tape roll and sends it spinning.{pause}GM chases the roll around the room while it gathers dust and one event flyer.{pause}The flyer now advertises movie night with a tasteful blue adhesive border.

nodes.name: Coat 05
nodes.speaker: GM
nodes.dialogue: We should remove the switch plate before painting, like the instructions say.{pause}Mk-II agrees, then produces a tool kit organized by battlefield urgency instead of size.{pause}The smallest screwdriver is filed under surrender prevention and takes six minutes to locate.{pause}By then GM has unscrewed the plate with a coin from the vending machine.

nodes.name: Coat 06
nodes.speaker: Narrator
nodes.dialogue: They spread the drop cloth and discover it is smaller than the wall by one awkward meter.{pause}Mk-II overlaps it with three newspapers, two cardboard boxes, and the movie schedule.{pause}GM rescues the schedule before it becomes part of the protective flooring system.{pause}A corner of bare floor remains exposed and immediately feels like the center of destiny.

nodes.name: Coat 07
nodes.speaker: Mk-II
nodes.dialogue: The blue wall needs primer, patience, and a refusal to repeat earlier color decisions.{pause}GM says blue is not morally wrong; it only clashes with the borrowed projector screen.{pause}Mk-II stares at the wall until GM changes the subject to brush selection.{pause}They choose one wide roller and one tiny brush shaped like a nervous mustache.

nodes.name: Coat 08
nodes.speaker: SYSTEM
nodes.dialogue: The first paint can opens with a soft click and the room becomes extremely attentive.{pause}Mk-II stirs clockwise for twelve turns, then counterclockwise for balance and symbolism.{pause}GM asks whether symbolism affects drying time; Mk-II says only when ignored.{pause}A single white drop lands on the exposed floor corner and wins destiny immediately.

nodes.name: Coat 09
nodes.speaker: GM
nodes.dialogue: We have not touched the wall and already need the emergency damp rag.{pause}Mk-II deploys three rags, labels the spill contained, and salutes the clean patch.{pause}The patch is now cleaner than the surrounding floor and therefore much more visible.{pause}GM adds clean entire floor to a list titled Consequences of Volunteering.

nodes.name: Coat 10
nodes.speaker: Mk-II
nodes.dialogue: Before the first coat, we must choose a working style suited to two very different frames.{pause}One method divides the wall into measured sectors with strict brush assignments.{pause}The other pairs roller and detail brush so both painters move together.{pause}GM says either method is fine if it eventually includes actual paint on the wall.

nodes.name: Coat Grid 1
nodes.speaker: Mk-II
nodes.dialogue: Mk-II marks the wall into a precise grid using tape, ruler, and unnecessary coordinates.{pause}GM receives sectors B4 through D7, plus a laminated map and emergency alternate route.{pause}The first roller stroke crosses two sector borders and triggers a brief jurisdiction debate.{pause}They solve it by declaring wet paint exempt from administrative boundaries.

nodes.name: Coat Grid 2
nodes.speaker: GM
nodes.dialogue: The grid makes every patch measurable, but it also creates forty-two tempting little finish lines.{pause}Mk-II completes his sectors with perfect edges and checks them using a pocket flashlight.{pause}GM completes fewer sectors but paints around the outlet without sealing it forever.{pause}They compare results and award both methods provisional approval with notes.

nodes.name: Coat Pair 1
nodes.speaker: GM
nodes.dialogue: GM rolls broad white lanes while Mk-II follows with the tiny mustache brush.{pause}Their rhythm works until Mk-II tries to detail a drip while GM is still rolling upward.{pause}The handles cross, the tray tilts, and both freeze like a very polite sculpture.{pause}They uncross one joint at a time and save all but one chair leg.

nodes.name: Coat Pair 2
nodes.speaker: Mk-II
nodes.dialogue: Working together produces uneven speed but surprisingly even coverage.{pause}GM calls the rescued chair leg an accent; Mk-II calls it an unresolved surface incident.{pause}They rotate the chair so the white leg faces the wall and cannot testify.{pause}The first painted section dries while they agree never to mention the sculpture.

nodes.name: Coat 11
nodes.speaker: Narrator
nodes.dialogue: The ventilation tune returns as the team steps back from the first broad field of white.{pause}Measured sectors or paired strokes, the result is undeniably brighter and only slightly striped.{pause}The original blue still shows through like a memory refusing to miss movie night.{pause}Mk-II opens the second can with the calm of someone who expected resistance.

nodes.name: Coat 12
nodes.speaker: GM
nodes.dialogue: The instructions say to wait until the first coat is dry to the touch.{pause}Mk-II asks whose touch qualifies and whether a sensor reading would be more objective.{pause}GM tests a low corner with one finger and leaves a perfect fingerprint in the paint.{pause}Mk-II labels it authorized sample point and draws a tiny square around it.

nodes.name: Coat 13
nodes.speaker: SYSTEM
nodes.dialogue: Drying time becomes the longest eighteen minutes in community hall history.{pause}They watch the wall, rearrange brushes, and count the chairs needed for movie night.{pause}Mk-II tells GM that changing colors can be simple if everyone stops narrating it.{pause}GM nods and offers half a sandwich without asking any follow-up question.

nodes.name: Coat 14
nodes.speaker: Mk-II
nodes.dialogue: The sandwich is cut diagonally, which Mk-II identifies as structurally superior.{pause}GM says it was cut that way because the lunch box is too small for rectangles.{pause}For a quiet minute they sit beneath the unfinished wall and listen to paint dry.{pause}The blue showing through seems less like an enemy and more like the first draft.

nodes.name: Coat 15
nodes.speaker: Narrator
nodes.dialogue: A volunteer opens the door, sees two tiny robots staring at a wall, and backs out.{pause}The sudden draft lifts the newspaper flooring and sends it flapping into the wet paint.{pause}Mk-II catches one corner; GM catches another; the movie schedule catches the middle.{pause}They peel it free and discover a reversed list of showtimes printed in white.

nodes.name: Coat 16
nodes.speaker: GM
nodes.dialogue: That looks almost intentional, like ghost writing for people who stand very close.{pause}Mk-II insists the wall is not becoming a mural and smooths the print with his roller.{pause}The effort erases most letters but leaves three pale stars and half a moon.{pause}GM quietly photographs them before the second coat makes the evidence disappear.

nodes.name: Coat 17
nodes.speaker: Mk-II
nodes.dialogue: Second coat begins with longer strokes, lighter pressure, and no symbolic stirring.{pause}The paint covers the blue much better, which Mk-II pretends was always guaranteed.{pause}GM works around the pale stars and asks whether they should preserve one.{pause}Mk-II paints within a brush width of the smallest star, then changes the subject.

nodes.name: Coat 18
nodes.speaker: SYSTEM
nodes.dialogue: Mk-II's vents engage to speed drying and immediately alter local weather.{pause}Loose tape rises first, followed by newspaper, dust, and the sandwich wrapper.{pause}A mist of white paint arcs across the wall in a surprisingly elegant curve.{pause}GM dives for the third can and hugs it like a valuable but unhelpful child.

nodes.name: Coat 19
nodes.speaker: GM
nodes.dialogue: Ventilation is useful when the air is not carrying every loose object we own.{pause}Mk-II powers down and surveys the curve, which ends in a cluster of bright droplets.{pause}The pattern resembles a comet crossing the half-hidden stars from the movie schedule.{pause}Neither painter says mural, but both stand back far enough to see one.

nodes.name: Coat 20
nodes.speaker: Mk-II
nodes.dialogue: The primer march returns while Mk-II calculates how much paint remains in each can.{pause}Can one is empty, can two is low, and Emotional Reserve is still nearly full.{pause}GM asks why the third can has a warning label written in Mk-II's handwriting.{pause}Mk-II says the warning is personal and rotates the label toward the wall.

nodes.name: Coat 21
nodes.speaker: Narrator
nodes.dialogue: They remove the tape while the second coat is soft enough to release cleanly.{pause}One strip comes away perfectly; the next tears into twelve determined little flags.{pause}GM pulls each flag with tweezers as Mk-II counts down from twelve.{pause}At zero, the edge is straight except where one pale star touches the ceiling.

nodes.name: Coat 22
nodes.speaker: GM
nodes.dialogue: The hall manager calls to ask whether the room will be ready by seven.{pause}Mk-II says the wall is operational, pending final aesthetic doctrine and floor restoration.{pause}GM translates that into yes, then looks at the blue powdery footprints everywhere.{pause}The hall manager thanks them and mentions a children's space movie on tonight's program.

nodes.name: Coat 23
nodes.speaker: Mk-II
nodes.dialogue: A space movie does not automatically justify stars, comets, or unauthorized half moons.{pause}GM agrees while mixing a drop of leftover blue into a cup of white.{pause}The color becomes a soft silver-gray that perfectly matches the accidental comet tail.{pause}Mk-II watches the mixing stick for a long time before asking for the small brush.

nodes.name: Coat 24
nodes.speaker: Narrator
nodes.dialogue: They clean the floor together, including the patch that became too clean to ignore.{pause}The white chair leg receives three matching partners and can no longer provide testimony.{pause}Brushes soak in labeled jars while the wall waits for a final decision.{pause}The third can sits between them, open now, bright and impossibly full.

nodes.name: Coat 25
nodes.speaker: GM
nodes.dialogue: We can apply one perfect third coat and make the whole room calm and uniform.{pause}Or we can keep the comet, finish the stars, and call the splashes intentional.{pause}Mk-II touches the authorized sample square, now hidden beneath two layers of white.{pause}He says either finish can be honest if they choose it before the paint dries.

nodes.name: Coat 26
nodes.speaker: Mk-II
nodes.dialogue: They walk the room once more while the second coat settles into a soft shine.{pause}The comet begins near the window, crosses the longest wall, and ends beside the pantry.{pause}Every accidental star marks a place where someone laughed or reached too quickly.{pause}GM notices the plain corners make the bright marks easier to read, not harder.{pause}Mk-II writes that observation beneath the buried sample number on his clipboard.

nodes.name: Coat 27
nodes.speaker: GM
nodes.dialogue: The tenants return early and stop in the doorway before either painter can explain.{pause}One child finds a star at exactly her height and names it the Snack Cup Nebula.{pause}An older neighbor likes the quiet white wall where the afternoon light now spreads.{pause}Nobody agrees on one perfect room, but everyone points to a part they want to keep.{pause}Mk-II lowers the roller and listens until the hallway has finished voting aloud.

nodes.name: Coat 28
nodes.speaker: Mk-II
nodes.dialogue: A third coat would preserve the calm wall and cover every mark that missed the plan.{pause}A mural finish would preserve the shared mistakes and frame them with deliberate stars.{pause}GM sets one clean roller beside the small brushes so either choice can begin at once.{pause}The paint is still workable, the room is finally quiet, and the decision belongs here.{pause}Mk-II asks whether the room should hide its history or sign it together.

nodes.name: Coat A1
nodes.speaker: Mk-II
nodes.dialogue: Third coat. Precision over panic, even when the panic has a charming comet shape.{pause}Mk-II rolls from ceiling to floor while GM keeps the edge wet and the tray steady.{pause}The stars vanish one by one beneath a smooth field of warm, even white.{pause}Mk-II saves the smallest star for last, then covers it with one careful stroke.

nodes.name: Coat A2
nodes.speaker: GM
nodes.dialogue: The finished wall reflects the projector test without a ripple, stripe, or blue shadow.{pause}Chairs line up beneath it, all four legs matching after their emergency repaint.{pause}GM hangs the movie schedule beside the door instead of using it as flooring.{pause}Mk-II signs the volunteer sheet with a tiny white fingerprint next to his name.

nodes.name: Coat A3
nodes.speaker: SYSTEM
nodes.dialogue: Movie night begins, and the space film looks bright against the flawless new surface.{pause}During the quiet opening scene, Mk-II notices a pale star reflected from the exit sign.{pause}He nudges GM and points; GM nods without saying the obvious word.{pause}The wall is uniform, but it still knows what they almost painted there.

nodes.name: Coat A4
nodes.speaker: Narrator
nodes.dialogue: The hall manager awards them a ribbon for Perfect Finish and a mop for next Saturday.{pause}Mk-II accepts both, then relabels Emotional Reserve as Community Hall Touch-Up Paint.{pause}GM frames the photograph of the accidental stars and hangs it in the supply closet.{pause}Under it, the saved warning label reads: OPEN ONLY AFTER THE SECOND DRAFT.

nodes.name: Coat B1
nodes.speaker: Mk-II
nodes.dialogue: Mk-II dips the small brush into silver-gray and extends the accidental comet tail.{pause}GM turns the remaining splashes into stars, planets, and one moon shaped like a sandwich.{pause}They preserve a strip of original blue as the night sky behind everything.{pause}For once, changing color does not require erasing every color that came before.

nodes.name: Coat B2
nodes.speaker: GM
nodes.dialogue: The third can supplies clouds, rocket trails, and a glowing border for the projector.{pause}Mk-II uses measured sectors to space the stars and paired strokes to soften the comet.{pause}Both earlier methods return, no longer competing, each useful in a different corner.{pause}The white chair becomes a tiny astronaut seat beneath the painted moon.

nodes.name: Coat B3
nodes.speaker: SYSTEM
nodes.dialogue: Children enter for movie night and immediately search the wall for favorite constellations.{pause}One child finds the reversed showtime numbers hidden inside a distant silver planet.{pause}Mk-II calls it an archival feature and gives GM full credit for preserving it.{pause}The projector screen covers half the mural, making the stars appear to continue beyond it.

nodes.name: Coat B4
nodes.speaker: Narrator
nodes.dialogue: The hall awards them Accidental Masterpiece and the only ribbon without wet paint.{pause}Mk-II crosses out accidental, then writes collaboratively discovered in smaller letters.{pause}GM keeps the tiny mustache brush as a reminder that details can redirect a whole wall.{pause}The empty third can becomes a popcorn bucket, which is finally an appropriate use of{pause}reserve.
